conventions.units: metres, seconds and metres per second; angles in degrees where a key ends in Deg; fov is the vertical field of view in degrees
conventions.frame: right-handed, +Y up, +X west (toward the Pacific), +Z north (toward Marin); mean sea level and the water surface at Y = 0; origin on the bridge centreline midway between the towers
conventions.colours: sRGB unless a key says linear
conventions.generated: lanes[].entry, lanes[].exit and lanes[].polyline are computed from the bridge's Roadway surface by scripts/layout.ts --write and verified by --check and at staging; everything else is authored
conventions.behaviour: BEHAVIOUR.md beside this file specifies traffic, driving, flights and fog-bank drift for reimplementation in another engine

jointPlates.notes: Fix round 3 item 0. The four expansion-joint plates (bridge review 3) lie 1.5 mm above the Roadway, which runs on beneath them, so at range a 24-bit depth buffer cannot separate the two and the plates blink. When the bridge loads, their material (used by nothing else) takes this polygon offset toward the camera; the GLB is not changed.

bridge.notes: Dimensions measured from the bridge's review-2 runtime GLB; suspender planes are |x| 13.43 to 14.0 for |z| <= 960. obstructionNodes are the node-name prefixes that the chase camera and flights keep clear of.

placements.notes: farModel replaces model beyond tiers.json features.*.bridgeFarSwitch metres from the camera
tile GLBs are authored in scene coordinates; each tier loads the level set scene.json terrain.sets names
not placed until the viewer drives; it joins lane nb-middle at driving.json start

approaches.notes: Fix round 2 (review 2 item 1): US 101 continues off both anchorages. Per end the alignment (PIs with circular curves, scene x/z), the modelled length, the join of the structure profile with the at-grade profile, the structures, the car's turnaround and the end's dissolve are authored; start, profile, segments, centreline and deviation are derived from the bridge GLB's Roadway end and the canonical near terrain by scripts/layout.ts --write and checked by --check (BEHAVIOUR.md 'Approach roads').

crossSection.notes: Shared by both approaches. The carriageway (+-9.4488), lane lines, edge lines and median continue the deck's; shoulders run to concrete barriers whose outer faces line up with the deck walkways' outer edge (12.5 m). The deck's curbs, walkways and railings end at the anchorage, where a short concrete ramp takes the walkways (0.22 m above the road) down to the shoulder. Materials: the bridge GLB's Asphalt, RoadMarkings and Concrete. Columns and abutment walls run down to supports.footing, below the ground everywhere along the approaches; the terrain hides what lies under it.

south.notes: South over the Presidio toward the toll plaza: the viaduct off the south anchorage, the plaza stretch at grade, an overpass over the dip at Lincoln Boulevard, then the Presidio Parkway past the crest into the pocket behind the plateau rim, where the road ends (the terrain frame's modelled stretch; the real road continues onto the Presidio Viaduct).

structures.note: over the dip at Lincoln Boulevard

imagery.notes: Road centre points read from the terrain imagery (paved-band centres every 20 to 25 m). The toll plaza (stations about 370 to 450) widens the paved area to the west, so its band centre is not the road centre and it carries no reference.

north.notes: North off the north anchorage on a viaduct, into the cut past the vista point, up the Waldo grade to the road's end beyond the second curve, out of sight of the deck.

cuts.notes: The Marin climb (review 3 item 3). North of the overpass our near terrain west of the climb (+x) rises 10 to 14 m within 20 m of the centreline and about 40 m by 45 m, and our imagery shows the cut there as pale mottled scrub and soil from about s 945 onward, x 15 to 50; a bright line at x 12 to 13 with a dark band at x 14.5 to 16 from s 955 onward is read as a low retaining wall at the toe and its shadow (no such line where the corridor's other cuts are, all under 1.5 m deep). The corridor's 1:1 cut slope, gentler than this terrain, had cut up to 11 m into it with a smeared face out to x 45. The benched faces (2 m of rise per m, a 2.5 m bench every 10 m of rise: 1.33 m per m overall, near the terrain's own average) keep the cut within about 5 m of the natural surface and meet it by x 40 to 46. Beyond the road's end (s 980) the terrain fades back to the natural surface, which buries the wall's north end. Scrub colours: the imagery's mean colours of the 10-35 % and 65-90 % luma bands over the region (tests/tools/dressing-imagery.ts).

imagery.notes: Road centre points read from the terrain imagery; one band centre in the wide paved area at the vista point turnoff (317.6, 1676.1) is left out for the same reason as the south toll plaza.

dressing.notes: Fix round 3 (golden-gate-scene/SCENE-REVIEW-3.md items 1 to 5): the approaches' dressing, placed from our own terrain imagery only (tests/tools/dressing-imagery.ts draws it over the imagery and measures it). Positions are approach stations s (m from the bridge's road end) and lane offsets x (m, the lanes' convention: + is the southbound lanes' side); heights are above the road at the station. Materials: the bridge GLB's Asphalt, RoadMarkings, Concrete and LampGlass, and the scene's own neutral painted steel (paint). No signage, text, numbers or logos anywhere.

paint.notes: The scene's own neutral painted steel (sRGB): the toll plaza canopy and columns and the approaches' light standards (poles, arms and cobra heads).

plaza.notes: The toll plaza (review 3 item 1) south of the south pylons. From the imagery: a flat canopy across the road with its extra width on the southbound (+x) side, the roadway fanning out to it and back. The six lanes run straight through; the extra width is paved area only (no traffic). Toll islands under the canopy: one on each shoulder, one on the median line (0.6 m wide, clear of the inner lanes' cars) and four in the extra width; none between the through lanes, which the traffic uses at the deck's 3.1 m spacing. Two rows of slender columns stand on every island. The median barrier runs from the deck to the plaza, where the centre toll island takes over, and resumes after it (medianGap: it slopes down to the road over the approach joint taper before gap[0] and back up after gap[1]; review 3 item 4). The paved edge on the +x side runs from the approach's 12 m out to pavedTo between fan[1] and fan[2], with smoothstep transitions from fan[0] and back to fan[3]; its barrier and the terrain bed follow it.

imagery.notes: Read from the staged near albedo mosaic (0.98 m per texel): the canopy roof's bright outline. The orthophoto shows an object h m up displaced east (-X) by approaches.south.imagery.displacement x h, here 2.1 m further along the approach and 2.9 m toward -x for the 6.2 m roof.

vista.notes: Vista Point (review 3 item 2), east of the northbound lanes beside the north anchorage, traced on maps drawn from our own near albedo imagery (about 0.98 m per texel) and checked against the imagery's own edges (tests/tools/dressing-imagery.ts): the lot's pale paved outline, its planted centre island (the outer edge of its planting; the pale paths among the planting belong to the island), the throat at its north-west corner where it meets the northbound shoulder, and the parked cars along the kerbs and the wall. Stations s and lane offsets x on the north approach (+ the southbound lanes' side, so the lot is at negative x). The lot is flat at `level`, the mean of the near terrain inside the outline (a least-squares plane there has grades under 0.4 % and residuals of -0.5 to +0.5 m at the 5th and 95th percentiles); the terrain is held `pavement` below it under the lot and throat (./corridor pads). Asphalt with a kerb on every edge but the throat's, the planted island as a kerbed opening onto the terrain (its imagery shows the planting), the low overlook wall along the south end facing the bridge (at the paving's outer edge, where the imagery shows the wall's shadow), stall lines along four kerbs and the wall, and a few static parked cars from the traffic set. The throat ramps from the shoulder to the lot through a gap in the edge barrier. The service road along the highway and the loop to the east are in the imagery but not modelled; the imagery shows no building (the only candidate, 9.5 x 3.5 m in a bus bay at s 352 to 362, reads as a parked coach), so there is no restroom block.

throat.notes: The outline edge from vertex `edge` to the next is the throat's lot end; the throat runs from it straight to the paved edge, and the edge barrier on that side has a gap over the same stations.

wall.notes: Outline vertices from `from` forward (wrapping) to `to`: the south-east end facing the bridge. Concrete, in place of the kerb there.

stalls.notes: Stall lines every `width` along the kerb polylines, or the overlook wall's, where the imagery shows parked cars (outline or planter vertices `from` forward to `to`), `depth` into the lot from the kerb's or the wall's face, painted like the road's lines.

lights.notes: Highway light standards (review 3 item 4): plain cobra-head standards on both approaches' edge barriers, in pairs 91.44 m apart, the deck lamps' own spacing (300 ft) continued beyond the deck's last pair (at |z| 1005.84, 27.14 m short of each road end), so the first approach pair stands at s 64.30. A painted-steel pole (the scene's own paint, not the bridge's) rises from the barrier's top to an arm reaching 2.6 m over the shoulder and a cobra head whose lens (the bridge's LampGlass, lit with the deck lamps) is 10 m above the road. None within 3 m of a barrier opening on its side (Vista Point's throat), of the plaza canopy or of where the barriers begin to taper before the dissolve. Tiered like the deck lamps, which both bridge representations carry: the near representation has every standard, the far representation (beyond the far switch) those up to s 400 m, near the deck lamps' line. The deck's own lamp posts are the bridge GLB's and unchanged.

vegetation.notes: Vegetation impostors (review 3 item 5): cross cards where our own terrain imagery shows canopy within `reach` m of an approach's centreline (the Presidio forest south, the headland scrub and groves north), near representation only. Candidates lie on a world grid per kind, `spacing` m, each jittered within its cell and kept at the feature level's density (tiers.json features vegetation). None stands nearer the road than the edge barrier's outer face (out with the plaza's widening) plus `clear` m plus its half width, short of the deck end by its half width plus `clear`, in Vista Point's lot outside its planted island, over a benched cut, or on ground below `ground` m (water and beach). The GPU keeps a candidate where the imagery's canopy score at its root exceeds its seed: the imagery's colour over `footprint` m (sRGB 0-255) through each class's ramps (from, to; smoothstep): trees by green over red and luma, scrub by green over blue, luma and green over red where trees do not score. The card takes that colour. Heights and widths per kind are ranges (m); `sink` is the share of its height a card sinks below its root. Classes calibrated over the imagery: the Presidio forest reads green over red 12 to 19 at luma 67 to 115 with blue near green; the headland scrub is yellow-green (green over blue 15 to 29) at luma 90 to 105; dry grass is red over green; the sports fields' lawn reads green over red about 8 and luma 107.

orbit.notes: the orbit target stays inside |x|, |z| <= targetBounds and targetMinY..targetMaxY; the camera keeps clearance above terrain and water

chase.notes: spring-arm chase camera behind the driven car; a sphere of castRadius is cast from the car to the camera against the bridge obstruction nodes and the camera moves in to pad before any hit, never closer than minDistance; |x| stays within maxAbsX, inside the suspender planes; a pinch or the mouse wheel scales distance and height by a factor within zoom (times exp(zoomRate x the kit's zoom input) each frame; 1 on entering the car); a one-finger or mouse drag swings the camera around the car and it returns behind it after three seconds (the kit's orbit offset)

flights.interpolation: centripetal Catmull-Rom through the keys, position and target as separate curves, parameterised uniformly by key index
flights.easing: quadratic ease-in-out over the whole flight (u < 0.5: 2u^2, else 1 - (2 - 2u)^2 / 2), or smoothstep (3u^2 - 2u^3) where a flight names it; the eased value selects the key segment and the position within it
flights.timing: a key's seconds is the time from the previous key in eased time; keys without seconds share the flight's remaining time equally

paths.name: deck-run
paths.label: Deck run
paths.notes: 4.5 m over the median (above every vehicle, below the tower portals), looking 40 m ahead at 3 m; after the north tower it climbs over the deck and the north anchorage, crossing the east cable only north of z = 960 where the cable is below 74 m, turns right over the water east of the anchorage (never over the Marin headland, whose imagery seam at x = 0 and 1 m texels filled the old 70 % frame: fix round 1) and ends looking back at the span. Deck heights are the Roadway's at x = 0 (scripts/layout.ts --heights).

fogBanks.notes: Low fog banks west of the Gate, in the strait and over the headlands. Puffs are camera-facing sprites generated from the seed (BEHAVIOUR.md) and drift toward -X, wrapping between wrap.west and wrap.east. Opacity is presets.json banks; the count of banks is tiers.json features.*.fogBanks (the first N).

bridgeLamps.rule: emissive intensity = the authored emissive intensity x lamps

vehicleLamps.rule: emissive = authored emissive colour x mix(gain[0], gain[1], lights); brake lamps are further scaled by mix(brakeOff, 1, braking); taillight emissive is scaled down so its largest channel is at most taillightPeak; parked vehicles (dressing.vista.cars) have every lamp off
